title: fix(pm): stop check-widening-tells T2 keying on a continuation operator, and price a false positive honestly
body:
Part of #16822

`check:pm-widening-tells`' T2 read two variables as widening evidence that carry no
information about widening. Both are repaired here, in the matcher, and the docblock
sentence that priced a false positive at "one word in the claim comment" is corrected.

## Both instances, and why both

The card was filed on one instance; the `os-sales` comment reports a second with a
**different failure mode**, and repairing only the first would leave the sharper one
live and the card reading as closed.

| | instance 1 (objectui PR #8540) | instance 2 (objectui PR #8544) |
|---|---|---|
| arm | `BARE_STRING_ELEMENT` | `CLOSED_SET_OPENER` |
| matched | the first fragment of a `+`-concatenated prose string | three genuine `z.discriminatedUnion('type', [` declarations |
| spurious? | yes — not a set member at all | **no** — it saw exactly what it was built to see |
| honest escape | respell the prose | **none** |

Instance 2 is not a false positive: the matcher fires on the constructor keyword
whether the rewrite widens or narrows, and a flat `z.union` → `z.discriminatedUnion`
conversion **cannot** widen (the discriminated form tries exactly one arm where the
flat form tried all ⇒ its accept set is a subset). So the two repairs are different
shapes, and neither is "T2 is wrong": `SCHEMA_PROPERTY` (T1), `BARE_SCHEMA_ARM` and
`JSON_STRING_ROW` declined correctly on both diffs and are untouched.

## The instrument, reproduced before and after — on the real diffs, not fixtures

`objectstack-ai/objectui` was fetched read-only and the two PR diffs were driven
through C5's own input (`splitUnifiedDiff` → `wideningRefusal({declaration:'no',
repo:'objectstack-ai/objectui'})`). Before, at the heads the card names:

```
=== pr8540 @ 63c9bd239 — 5 changed file(s) ===
state=refused  exit=4  tells=1
  ✗ T2 packages/types/src/zod/feedback.zod.ts:84 — a new member of a closed set …
    + 'RETIRED (objectui#8338, ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove) — `action` had two published faces whose '
=== pr8544 @ ae6886dde — 9 changed file(s) ===
state=refused  exit=4  tells=3
  ✗ T2 packages/types/src/zod/crud.zod.ts:210      + export const CRUDComponentSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  ✗ T2 packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts:392     + export const AnyComponentSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
  ✗ T2 packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts:1277 + export const ObjectQLComponentSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('type', [
```

Row for row the four readings both comments report. After: `state=clean exit=0
tells=0` on both, and no other row moved — the delta is exactly those four.

**The eight-fragment arithmetic, which is the actual instrument.** The message has
eight fragments and exactly one tell fired, because fragments 2-8 begin `+ '…'` and
`^[ \t]*'` cannot match a leading `+`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| as written (first fragment on its own line) | **1 tell** | 0 |
| the identical string, first fragment moved up onto the calling line | 0 | 0 |

The two spellings of one string now agree. That is the whole claim: the tell keyed on
the accidental absence of a continuation operator, not on anything semantic.

## What changed, and which direction each refinement fails in

Both refinements read only bytes the hunk already carries — an added line's
neighbours on the new-file side, and what the same hunk removed. **⛔ Neither
recovers block state and neither claims direction.** The docblock's warning stands
unweakened: a hunk is a fragment, this is a tell and never a proof.

1. **A fragment of a multi-line string concatenation is not a bare element.** The
   continuation operator is now read on *both* sides (`+ 'more'` opening the next
   line, and `'prose ' +` ending the previous one — both spellings are in the tree).
   Measured 2026-09-08 over `packages/spec/src/**`: of 6,035 lines matching the
   bare-element shape, **1,707** are followed by a `+ '…'` continuation and **479**
   follow a line ending in `+` — 2,186 prose fragments on the surface T2 polices.
   ⭐ **Bounded in-place fix, named:** this reading is a property of the LINE, not of
   one tell, so it is applied once — which also retires the same accidental variable
   on T4's bare-element arm, where the ledger's waiver rows put 116 measured prose
   continuations on a registry surface. Same defect class, same instrument, no new
   verification surface. ⛔ Only the bare-STRING shape is declined: the keyed head of
   the same prose (`reason: 'Pre-gate synonym … ' +`) still reads as T4, pinned.
2. **An opener that re-declares the same binding adds no value.** An opener whose
   list opens on a *later* line declares no member; when the same hunk removes an
   opener with the identical binding prefix, the set already existed, and its
   members are still read one line each by the member tells.

**Failure directions, stated rather than implied.** Both decline only on *positive*
evidence: no neighbour, no paired removal, different hunk, different binding prefix ⇒
the tell still fires. The one quiet direction added is named in the header: a
closed-set MEMBER spelled as a multi-line concatenation (`'be'` / `+ 'ta',`) is now
declined. Measured over `packages/spec/src/**` + `packages/runtime/src/**`: of 4,957
member lines in 401 array/closed-set blocks, the 116 multi-line concatenations are
all property VALUES (the ledger waiver rows' `reason:` prose); no member is spelled
that way.

## `:68` — the price, corrected

```
:68  * the remedy is one word in the claim comment — never a weakened rule here.
```

Replaced with the price actually charged: C5's exit-0 condition is *"no tell, **or the
declaration is not `no`**"*, so the only word that clears a false tell is flipping
`Clause-②: no` → `yes` — recording a widening that did not happen in a ledger read
later as evidence of direction, where it is indistinguishable from a real one.

⛔ The sentence's true half is restated, not dropped: **a tell may be narrowed only on
evidence the hunk actually carries, and never in a way that trades a loud failure for
a quiet one.** ⛔ Nothing here is a bypass: the #16349 ruling and the #16448 C5 row
stand, `--pair`'s non-zero exit stays a hard block, and no suppression carrier, label
or claim-line syntax is introduced.

## Ablation — the new cases can fail

Both refinements were disabled in turn, on disk, and the self-test re-run; the file
was restored from `HEAD` each time and the restoration proved by blob hash.

```
=== LEG: concat ===   on-disk blob 68ef435d…  (HEAD 6867b6e2…)   self-test exit: 1
  failing cases: 4    ✗ ⭐ an 8-fragment prose ARGUMENT is not a closed-set member …
  restored: git diff HEAD is EMPTY; blob 6867b6e2d765aa0d0ae3a824ff69ad398a70b6e4
=== LEG: opener ===   on-disk blob 4562d6dc…  (HEAD 6867b6e2…)   self-test exit: 1
  failing cases: 2    ✗ ⭐ an opener that RE-DECLARES the set the same hunk removed …
  restored: git diff HEAD is EMPTY; blob 6867b6e2d765aa0d0ae3a824ff69ad398a70b6e4
```

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 35 families; all 35 run, all
exit 0, reconciled: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 35 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 35
run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.` Headline rows:

```
pnpm check:pm-widening-tells    exit=0   150 cases pass (131 before + 19 new)
pnpm check:pm-clause2-carriers  exit=0   299 cases pass
pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates    exit=0
pnpm check:nul-bytes            exit=0
pnpm check:pm-governed-prose    exit=0
```

Lint is a **declared narrowing**, at `82c5899bbe`: `eslint --no-inline-config
--format json` over the 2 files this diff changes — 2 files linted, 0 errors, 0
warnings. Inspected population read from ESLint's own config resolution
(`isPathIgnored` over `git ls-files`): 6,379 files. Invariance: this repo runs one
`eslint.config.mjs` which enables no type-aware linting for any file (its own header
records the measurement), so a diff confined to these two files cannot move an
untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run.

## 验收备注

- `skip-changeset`: nothing published moves — the root package is `private: true`,
  no package's `files[]` ships `scripts/`, and `scripts/pm/**` is tooling.
- ⚠️ **File-surface deviation, declared.** The claim allowed
  `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` "only if C5's exit condition must move". It does not
  move, and it did not. What was edited there is the **twin of the repaired
  sentence** in `c5WideningTell`'s docblock — "a false positive costs the author one
  word in the claim comment" — in the file that actually prints the C5 row. Comment
  bytes only; `needsWideningRead`, `pairWidening`, `c5WideningTell` and the exit
  register are untouched, and its 299-case self-test is green. Leaving the twin would
  route the next reader down the path triage named.
- ⚠️ Noted, not filed: `REFUSAL_SENTENCE` offers two doors ("re-declare `yes` **or
  explain in the claim**"), and C5's mechanical exit-0 condition honours only the
  first. Recorded here, ⛔ not changed — the sentence is quoted from #16448 and
  changing it is a ruling's business, not a matcher repair's.
- ⚠️ The routing tension recorded on the card (`scripts/pm/**` → `domain:skills` vs
  this card's `domain:devx`) is untouched: no label was changed.
- Reproduction note: objectui is read-only to this session (git reads, no API), so
  `--pair 8540` / `--pair 8544` were **not** re-run end to end; C5's diff half was
  driven directly on both PR diffs at the heads the card names.
